steps.text: In a medium bowl, cream together butter and 1 cup sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in egg, corn syrup, and lemon extract. Stir in flour, baking soda, and baking powder. Cover dough, and chill in the refrigerator at least 1 hour.

Preheat oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Line a cookie sheet with parchment paper. Roll chilled dough into walnut sized balls. Roll balls in remaining sugar, and place on the prepared cookie sheet.
Bake 12 minutes in the preheated oven, or until lightly browned.

review.reviewBody: Great tasting cookie. I used a tsp. of fresh lemon juice, and a tbs. of lemon zest (omitting the lemon extract). Excellent. After trying these, I have also decided to skip the rolling in sugar step, and just dust the cooled cookies with powdered sugar. The powdered sugar will nestle nicely into the surface of this cookie! Even though I made some slight alterations, I give these cookies 5 stars because they are sooo easy to prepare, quick to cook, and are incredibly easy to transport. It's crisp, yet chewy, allowing them to be packaged in any way. Mahalo nui loa!

I would double, if not triple, the lemon extract. Also, if anyone is wondering why there are discrepancies in the reviews as to the texture: if you want a crisp cookie, use lemon extract, not lemon juice. The acid in lemon juice will react with the baking soda to create a leavening agent, giving you chewy cookies. But, as others have said, these cookies are quite beautiful =)

These are delicious simple to make cookies I would double the lemon extract add a pinch of salt but otherwise they are simply delicious chili on the inside with just the right amount of Chris on the exterior I used a simple cookie scoop to make them into the small balls if you’re cooking on convection I recommend about eight minutes cook time

As everyone is saying- needs more lemon! I tasted the dough until I got the taste I was after and ended up adding 4 teaspoons total of lemon extract (instead of 1t) PLUS fresh lemon rind from 2 lemons- they were VERY lemony then, which I love, but 3 teaspoons should be plenty for normal folks who don't need their tastebuds exploded like I do. 
 Also, I loathe corn syrup, it is the most unhealthy food in the world, so I used 1T honey instead of the called for 2T corn syrup- worked great to make the cookies a little chewy, which is nice for this type of cookie. 
 I recommend baking this cookie until *just* cooked. They are very easy to under bake or over bake. I literally just sit in front of my oven with the oven light on and watch them for three minutes, turn them around so they bake evenly...and then wait until just cooked. 
 Perfect cookie baking is an art form, and one I have not yet mastered, but these are my tips and I hope they help you. I didn't add the extra sugar to roll in because they are already soooo sweet. I also added some lavender leaves.

These are so delectable! I read some of the reviews after I had prepared the cookie dough and put it in the fridge for an hour and ten minutes. You definitely want to refrigerate the dough to have it very firm when it goes into the oven. This will keep them from completely melting as soon as they go in and cut down on the spreading. I noticed some reviewers said that they didn't have lemon extract so they used lemon juice and therefore there was not enough lemon flavor in the finished cookies. The lemon extract and fresh lemon juice are not at all the same thing. The extract is much more concentrated and the one teaspoon of lemon extract gives this cookie the perfect amount of lemony deliciousness! I had a fresh bottle of Watkin's lemon extract that I used one teaspoon of. I didn't roll the cookies in extra sugar and they sure don't need that! They are perfectly sweet without the added rolling in sugar! I used a walnut sized cookie scoop that made short work of getting the dough balls on the parchment covered cookie sheets. Also, using the cookie scoop prevents the heat from your hands melting/softening the butter in the dough. The cookies were done in 12 minutes and they didn't spread into each other. My hubby said these cookies are most delicious and I have to completely agree! This is a lovely, lemony cookie that would go beautifully with a nice cuppa tea! Update: I tried two teaspoons of the lemon extract this time to see how that was as we love lemon flav

This is great. Still not enough lemon for my mother, but I could always make a lemon curd for her...

I used 3 tsp of lemon extract and added 1 tsp of lemon peel.

Also, I made a simple syrup since I did not have any light corn syrup. (What did have was dark corn syrup that expired in Oct 2016....oops.)

Even though they're not lemony enough for my mother, it hasn't stopped her from eating them. Haha. My dad even likes them well enough and he's not a sweet-eater like Mom and I are.

I suggest using a 1/2 Tbsp to scoop out the dough.

I will be making these again.

A few key changes brought these up to five star status! I doubled the lemon extract, added a tsp. of fresh lemon zest, and added several drops of yellow food coloring to the wet ingredients. I also made my own lemon sugar to roll them in, by adding lemon extract and yellow food coloring to the sugar! I only rolled the top of the cookie, as I didn't want them to be overly sweet. I didn't have parchment paper, I used cooking-spray and a light dusting of flour on the sheet, and they didn't stick at all. Also, I only had unsalted butter, so I added 1/4 tsp of salt to the dry ingredients. My dough was easy to handle after 15 minutes in the freezer. This cookie is delicious, and with the changes I added, is a real keeper. Thanks for sharing!

These are really very good. I had to make a variation on the recipe, because I live in Guatemala and lemons, as we know them, don't exist here. I used the zest and juice from a large lime instead of the extract, and as my husband put it, just tart enough and not too sweet. 

Because of the amount of juice in lime -- if you put one or two in the microwave for about 20 seconds you will get a lot more juice -- I added a couple tablespoons of coconut flour to the dough. Okay, and then I tossed in a handful of white chocolate chips. 

These baked up perfectly, not runny or spread out at all. They are softer than I usually like, but the flavor is perfect. I definitely recommend you use parchment paper. Let the cookies cool completely and they come off the paper easily. Otherwise, I had a few that wanted to stick even to the paper. These will definitely go into the box to be made again, as limes are plentiful and very inexpensive, and we love the flavor. Thank you for a great recipe.

I was craving a lemony treat and had some fresh lemons on hand so I made these cookies. They were so delicious! I made a few changes based on what I had on hand. Instead of lemon extract I used 2 tbs of fresh lemon juice and about a tsp or two of lemon zest (based off other reviews I wanted more lemon flavor). Instead of the corn syrup I used the same amount of honey. I didn't have any baking powder so I added an extra 1/4 tsp of baking soda and 1/2 tsp of cream of tartar. Instead of rolling in sugar I opted to dust with powdered sugar after cooling. These cookies were easy to make and so yummy. Just the right amount of lemon flavor and SO SOFT and chewy which is exactly what I wanted. I can't stop eating them!

With a couple of changes, this is the *perfect* base for a soft sugar cookie. Add 1/2 cup of flour, swap the extract for vanilla (lemon is good, but vanilla is better imo. I plan to try almond as well), and be sure to chill for at least 1.5 hours. Cookies come out soft and not too sweet. Be sure to watch for overbaking to prevent caramelization and a crunchy "ring" on the outside of the cookie -- the low temperature and short baking time is just right to keep the cookies soft and looking beautiful.

Very good recipe. I not only doubled the lemon extract and added lemon zest, but I reduced the sugar by 1/4. For a different twist, I ground freeze-dried blueberries in a food processor and mixed them with the remaining sugar and rolled the balls of dough in the mixture before baking. Very nice touch of blueberry.
I made these cookies adding the juice of a whole lemon, with the grated outer rind. The flavor was good but the cookies puffed up. I only used one teaspoon of baking soda. ??

I made half the recipe and got exactly 24 cookies. These were delicious. Crispy edges and softer centers. The dough was a bit on the sticky side. Maybe it was because I did not refrigerate my dough? Will be making these again. Thanks for sharing your recipe.
I also used fresh lemon juice and zest instead of lemon extract and lavendar syrup instead of corn syrup and it was delicious!
It is the best I have ever baked and my Family loves them Thanks For Sharing
I tripled the lemon extract for this recipe. In one instance, I added white chocolate chips to make them similar to Panera's lemon drop cookies.
super good, I actually forgot to chill them and they still worked perfectly! My friends and family also loved them, and a good majority of those people don't really like non-chocolate desserts.
the cookie is very good. It could have had a bit more lemony flavor, but it was good. I added about one teaspoon of lemon zest and fresh lemon juice.
My husband said, "YES!"
This recipe is perfect the way it is. And the dough freezes very well. Enjoy
